title: Owner roulette coverage slate — mini roster & one-off tracker
body:
Purpose: lightweight, one-page owner pool for short-lived cross-functional asks and cover swaps. Use this when you need someone to own a short task (<= 3 days) or to list temporary coverage for a route/endpoint. Not a replacement for long-term capacity planning; this is a sticky note that lives in Drive for quick handoffs.

How to use (quick):
- Add an entry row when you need coverage or a one-off owner.
- Keep descriptions short. Link to ticket if it exists.
- If >72h open, escalate to team lead and mark escalated.
- Weekly scrub: owner or next person in roster must update status.

Columns (interpreted below): ID | ITEM | OWNER (person) | TEAM | PRIORITY | STATUS | SLA (hrs) | NOTE | LINK

Rows (live sample):
1 | fallback-region-route validation spike | Marisol Ortega | product-ops | P2 | assigned | 48 | validate edge case where fallback chooses smaller model and increases latency; blockers: missing sim data | jira:OPS-4123
2 | dedicated-capacity-canary for eu-west pool | Benji Walker | infra | P1 | in_progress | 24 | short canary during weekday morning window; watch token burn | jira:INFRA-2291
3 | api-key-rotation follow-up (customer X) | Elena Park | customer-success | P2 | awaiting_input | 72 | CX provided partial logs, need SRE to confirm error class | confluence:cust-x-rotation-notes
4 | embeddings-cost-blitz quick audit | Ravi Singh | observability | P3 | assigned | 72 | quick sample of top 10 customers with >1M embed units/mo | slack:#billing-spikes
5 | private-deploy config sanity check (region swap) | Ana Kowalski | private-deployments | P2 | needs_owner | 48 | no owner yet — suggested owners: infra rotation or se on call | jira:PD-118
6 | rollout-fallback-policy tuning (canary stage) | Kai Nakamura | serving-runtime | P1 | in_progress | 24 | monitor regressions vs baseline prompts, fallback threshold to 0.6 | github:repo/PR-765
7 | SLA-cover-weekend (June 22-23) | Olivia Chen | site-reliability-engineering | P2 | assigned | 72 | backup: Marcus Rivera available as second-tier; confirm contact list | jira:SRE-332
8 | short customer demo: low-latency profile | Marcus Rivera | solutions-engineering | P2 | completed | 24 | demo run completed 2029-06-14; follow-up: deliver tuning notes | confluence:demo-low-latency
9 | transient-telemetry-gap (api/route:stage-7) | Priya Desai | observability | P1 | escalated | 8 | partial events dropped during 06/13 03:10-04:00 UTC; SRE investigating | jira:OBS-7008
10 | ad-hoc quantization-check (gptx-compat) | Benji Walker | applied-ml | P3 | needs_owner | 48 | quick spike to confirm int8 export behaviour; low priority | github:models/quant-spike

Notes and heuristics:
- Priority mapping: P1 = urgent (SLA <=24h), P2 = near-term (<=72h), P3 = low (<=1 week). Use commonsense.
- Status values: needs_owner, assigned, in_progress, awaiting_input, completed, escalated.
- owner can be a team rotation alias (e.g., infra-oncall) if no single person listed. When using alias, add contact in NOTE.
- If you link a Jira/PR, update that artifact when status changes (toggle link).

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Should we add an explicit 'backup' column? For now keep it in NOTE to avoid schema churn.
- Do weekly scrubs need a recurring calendar event or is team-specific ad-hoc better? Action: ask leads during next ops sync.

Next steps (short):
- Elena: finalize owner list and rotation aliases (due 2029-06-18).
- Ravi: run cost sample for embeddings and paste summary here (due 2029-06-17).
- Marisol: confirm fallback validation test data availability (due 2029-06-16).

Slack shorthand for updates: add +owner or +done in the row NOTE (e.g., "+Benji" or "+done 2029-06-14").

Historical log (brief):
- 2029-06-12 created as ad-hoc capture during ops sync.
- 2029-06-13 populated with initial 7 rows; added canary item.
- 2029-06-15 Ravi added embeddings sample row and Priya flagged telemetry issue.

If you find this tracker useful and want it templated: copy file name with date suffix and drop into same folder.

-- end of mini-tracker sheet (keep it lean)
